output.title: Why subscription sprawl survives in small teams
output.body:
Subscription sprawl usually survives in small teams because it gets treated as background admin. A tool is signed up for, the renewal date is noted somewhere, and then the note gets buried under invoices, emails, and everything else that was already waiting.

For an owner-operator, the real workflow decision is simple: do you have one place where every active subscription and renewal date is visible, or is the knowledge spread across inboxes and memory? If it is spread out, the first step is not automation. It is a one-time manual audit so you can build a clean list first. If the list is already tidy, a spreadsheet and a regular review may be enough.

That is the kind of bounded workflow Bareni looks for: one recurring task, one clear owner, and a control that fits the actual mess in front of you. If the workflow is recurring, repeatable, and tied to a measurable outcome, then AI can be part of the system. If not, it is usually better to keep it simple. Human approval still owns any cancellation or payment step. Tiny bit of unglamorous work, but that is often the point.
